definitions.gloss: Japanese-style; done in the Japanese manner
definitions.explanation: Designating something done in a distinctly Japanese way, in contrast to {西洋式|せいようしき} or {洋式|ようしき} (Western-style).

examples.japanese: {日本式|にほんしき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧。
{日本式|にほんしき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{経営|けいえい}→経営：02740_keiei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{独特|どくとく}→独特：01656_dokutoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{特徴|とくちょう}→特徴：03456_tokuchou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
⟦ローマ{字|じ}→ローマ字：11225_roomaji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{日本式|にほんしき}、ヘボン{式|しき}、{訓令|くんれい}{式|しき}⟦など→〜など：03095_nado⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{表記法|ひょうきほう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: For romaji there are several notations such as Nihon-shiki, Hepburn, and Kunrei-shiki.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧ (Japan) + the suffix {式|しき} (style, system). Often interchangeable with ⟦{和式|わしき}→和式：23138_washiki⟧, though ⟦{和式|わしき}→和式：23138_washiki⟧ is more common for everyday physical items (especially ⟦{和式|わしき}→和式：23138_washiki⟧⟦トイレ→トイレ：00818_toire⟧) and {日本式|にほんしき} is more common for abstract systems (management, education, romanization).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- As a noun modifier: {日本式|にほんしき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ + noun
- As a predicate: {日本式|にほんしき}だ / です

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{和式|わしき}→和式：23138_washiki⟧: Japanese-style — more common for physical objects/facilities
- ⟦{日本|にほん}{風|ふう}→日本風：26055_nihonfuu⟧: Japanese in feel — softer; a Japanese-like atmosphere or flavor
